title: Journey - Five Days of Peace - Day 5: Perfect peace

parts.style: warm, gentle welcome, steady and unhurried
parts.text: Welcome to Five Days of Peace. <short pause> This is day five, Perfect Peace. <short pause> It's the last day of this journey, and I'm glad you are here. <short pause> We have one step left... and it's the one where you get to stop holding yourself up.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Find something you can lean on. <short pause> The back of a chair. A wall. A pillow, or the arm of a sofa. <short pause> Don't give it your weight just yet. <short pause> Only know that it's there, behind you. <short pause> Let your breath come and go.

Worry keeps us very upright. <short pause> Even lying down, some part of us is sitting forward, braced, watching the door. <short pause> We are holding up the people we love, and the future, and ourselves. <short pause> And we call it being responsible. <short pause> But a body can't rest in that position... and neither can a soul.

Isaiah wrote down a song for God's people to sing. <short pause> It's about a strong city, with salvation for its walls. <short pause> And in the middle of that song, among all that stone, there is a line about the human mind. <short pause> It is Isaiah chapter twenty-six, verse three.

parts.style: reverent, very slow, reading scripture aloud
parts.text: Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: That word, stayed, means propped. <short pause> Held up by leaning on something stronger. <short pause> And where our Bible says perfect peace, the Hebrew simply says the word twice. <short pause> Shalom, shalom. <short pause> Peace, peace. <short pause> As if once were not enough for someone as tired as you.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: So now, let the wall have you. <short pause> Slowly, give your back to what is behind you. <short pause> A little weight. <short pause> A little more. <short pause> Feel the exact moment when you are no longer the one doing the holding. <short pause> Let your mind do the same thing, toward God. <short pause> It doesn't have to be empty. <short pause> It only has to lean.

parts.style: tender reassurance, slow, resting between sentences
parts.text: You will sit forward again. <short pause> Everybody does. <short pause> A stayed mind is not a mind that never moves. <short pause> It's a mind that knows where the wall is, and keeps coming back to rest on it. <short pause> Each return is trust... even the hundredth one.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: And you know the way back now. <short pause> We spread the letter out where He could read it. <short pause> We took off the heavy coat. <short pause> We turned our worry into asking, and thanks. <short pause> We drew the edges of one day. <short pause> And we leaned. <short pause> Let's walk through all five, slowly, and then once more as you would in a hard moment.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Turn your palms up. <short pause> Here it is. <short pause> Let your shoulders fall. <short pause> It's Yours. <short pause> Rest a hand on your heart. <short pause> Help me, and thank You. <short pause> Draw the small square. <short pause> Just today. <short pause> And lean back, all the way. <short pause> I lean on You.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Now a little more simply, the way you might in a waiting room, with no one noticing. <short pause> Palms... here it is. <short pause> Shoulders... it's Yours. <short pause> Heart... help me, and thank You. <short pause> Square... just today. <short pause> And lean... I lean on You.

parts.style: prayerful, slow, soft but clearly spoken
parts.text: Let's pray. <short pause> Lord, my strong city, I lay my weight on You. <short pause> Keep in perfect peace this mind that wanders and comes home. <short pause> When worry returns, remind my hands what to do. <short pause> And thank You that beneath every step I have learned, it was always You holding me. <short pause> Amen.

parts.style: warm, steady, slow sending, resting between phrases
parts.text: The journey ends here, and the way back stays open. <short pause> Five steps, less than a minute, as many times a day as you need. <short pause> Thank you for walking these days with me. <short pause> May the peace of God keep you... <short pause> peace, peace.
